thread:
Alex Chen: Heads up — seeing steady p90 latency + error-rate on /v1/generate in prod since ~00:04 UTC. Not a full SEV yet but paging threshold crossed for SLO-1. I'm primary until 04:00. Can someone pick secondary? /cc @Maya Patel
IncidentBot: Alert triggered: service=infra-inference, symptom=high-p90-latency, rule=p90>700ms for 3m. Created INC-20260084 severity=SEV2 (auto-created).
Maya Patel: I got secondary. Joining now and starting triage.
Samir Rao: Samir jumping in. Quick Q — customer impact? dashboards show most of the error-rate in us-west. If customers impacted, page prod-ops.
Alex Chen: Customer impact: a small subset of long-context requests seeing 502s and timeouts. Not global but affecting a few enterprise customers. Traces point to model queue spikes (ml-worker backlog). I've started runbook steps 1-3.
Samir Rao: Commands I'm running now:
```
# check queue depth
kubectl -n inference exec deploy/queue-watcher -- curl localhost:9090/metrics | grep queue_depth
# tail ml-worker logs
kubectl -n inference logs -l app=ml-worker -c worker --tail 200
```
Linh Tran: I can try a temporary routing canary to a smaller model variant for the long-context route. Suggest model-quant32 at 5% to start.
Alex Chen: Good plan. Paging/esc rules we should follow here: page primary immediately (0m), if no ack escalate to secondary at +5m, then to prod-ops group at +10m, then engage Eng-Platform (SEV leads) at +20m. Please document on the incident.
Maya Patel: Noted. I'm watching and will update INC-20260084 with affected customer list + current mitigations.
IncidentBot: INC-20260084: PagerDuty alert acknowledged by Maya Patel at 00:09 UTC.
Priya Singh: Priya from Platform — if you do routing changes, paste the exact patch and a rollback plan here. Also ensure we have a metrics snapshot before/after.
Linh Tran: Patch I'll apply (will verify in staging then canary in prod):
```
kubectl -n routing patch cm model-routes -p '{"data":{"long_context":"model-quant32:5,model-xxl:95"}}'
# verify
curl -s https://routing.internal/health | jq '.routes.long_context'
```
Alex Chen: Proceed with the 5% canary. I'll monitor p90 and error-rate for us-west. If error-rate > 1% for 10m we escalate to SEV1 and page SRE leads.
Samir Rao: Adding runbook link: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/latency-spike — follow the "reduce-queue-backpressure" steps, especially the "drain-workers" and "scale-down-large-models" subsections.
Maya Patel: Canary applied and verified. Initial traffic diverted 5% to model-quant32. After ~4 minutes p90 in us-west dropped from ~820ms -> ~420ms. Error count for long-context path down ~60%. Continuing to monitor.
Alex Chen: Great. Who is next handoff at 04:00? Need to make sure Jordan sees this before swap.
Priya Singh: On-call schedule shows Jordan Li takes 04:00-12:00 primary, secondary Samir Rao. Jordan has been paged. Rollback note: if canary worsens, revert patch with: `kubectl -n routing patch cm model-routes --type=json -p '[{"op":"replace","path":"/data/long_context","value":"model-xxl:100"}]'`
Jordan Li: Jordan here, will take the 04:00 handoff. I'll stay in the thread and verify stability at swap.
IncidentBot: INC-20260084: status updated -> MONITORING. Severity remains SEV2. Auto-close condition: traffic normal for 30m.
Alex Chen: We'll keep the incident open to monitor for the full 30m window post-stabilization. Thanks everyone for the quick canary. :thumbsup: 
Maya Patel: I'll update the incident timeline and include handoff notes for Jordan.
Samir Rao: Leaving a short checklist for the next primary: 1) confirm routing cm is stable; 2) check worker queue depths; 3) confirm telemetry for affected customer orgs.
Alex Chen: Perfect. I'll publish a short post-incident note in #postmortems if we need follow-up actions (model autoscale tuning, routing thresholds).
